title: Illinois v. Wardlow (2000)
key_points: Holding: Unprovoked, headlong flight on seeing police in a high-crime area can support reasonable suspicion for a stop.
officer_notes: Scenario: A man in an area known for open-air drug sales sees your marked unit and sprints away. You may stop him to investigate.
Takeaway: Presence in a high-crime area alone is not enough; flight plus location can be.
